turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A huge storm's forecast for Wednesday and I'm working out how to prepare.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Let me describe everything first, and then I'll ask for your thoughts.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I could buy a little generator in case the power goes, but they're expensive and noisy.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Or just stock up on torches, batteries, water and tinned food, and ride it out at home.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My mum lives inland and says we can stay with her, though it's a two hour drive with the kids.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And that's the last one. What do you think?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Stocking up is a good idea whatever you choose, it's cheap and useful. The generator only makes sense if long power cuts are common where you are. Your mum's place is the safest if the storm looks really serious.
